A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gaze-based mistake-detection work. All 16 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections A-B, are readable, and their text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on EPIC-Tent, HoloAssist, and IndustReal, alongside ablations, qualitative examples, and analyses involving ratings from 40 volunteers.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results, supplementary experiments, and analyses of action complexity, confidence, and action type.

M1.justification: The gaze-completion architecture, channel and correlation fusion, KL training loss, trajectory prediction, and four scoring functions are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use EPIC-Tent, HoloAssist, and IndustReal for the same tasks and scenarios. The action categories and volunteer-based complexity analysis are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Random, TimeSformer, C2F, GLC, and the same TrajREC and MoCoDAD variants. Removing discussion of joint hand/gaze keypoints does not remove those comparators from Table 2.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and sample counts, supervision settings, evaluation metrics, threshold selection, frame windows, and training settings remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the scoring/fusion ablations, prediction-length and threshold analyses, action-complexity/confidence/type analyses, and qualitative examples. Supplementary renumbering introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: The point-biserial correlations, chi-square/Cramer's V analysis, and p-value reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1-4 and v4 supplementary Tables 1-4, renumbered as Tables 5-8 in v5, retain identical entries and numerical values. The plotted distributions, threshold curve, and qualitative examples also match.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup and scoring equations are unchanged. The supplementary KL-loss equation is renumbered from (1) to (6), without changing its mathematics; no proofs or formal assumptions are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unsupervised mistake detection, gaze completion, benchmark improvements, useful action scenarios, and HoloAssist challenge ranking.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 removes the explanation that combining gaze with hand keypoints may hurt performance because gaze trajectories do not always align with hand movements. The supporting results remain in Table 2, and the broader applicability and limitation discussions are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, baseline adaptations, missing-keypoint handling, action categorization instructions, and code-access statements remain unchanged. Appendix citation placeholders are repaired, but no new technical settings or resource availability are disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the GazeSAM radiology example and citation with a broader visual-task statement citing Yao et al.'s teacher-generated spatial-attention work and Zhou et al.'s observer-gaze work. The main novelty and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 condenses portions of Section 4.4, repairs unresolved appendix citations, adds co-first-author attribution and acknowledgments, and updates cross-references. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 compacts the author block and adjusts page flow, including moving Figure 4 from PDF page 9 to page 8. Supplementary figures and tables receive continuous numbering, while their graphics, panels, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Repairing v4's unresolved appendix citations makes the supporting methods and comparisons easier to trace, while limited prose editing improves readability without changing the empirical evidence. These modest gains are partly offset by removing the explanation for poorer joint hand/gaze keypoint performance.
